9	## Five rules that apply at every point (board 0)
10	
11	1. **One word, one unit, always translated.** "Credits" (decided 2026-11-01), never coins, never tokens. A credit is explained once, in messages: "an Expert message is 5 credits, a Standard message is 1". Every balance is shown translated, "612 credits left. That is 612 Standard or 112 Expert messages", so nobody converts in their head. The Expert count leaves out credits that only Standard can spend: 612 credits of which 50 are free Standard messages is (612 − 50) / 5 = 112, not 122 (the first boards said 122; fixed in canvas version 70). A price never stands alone: "1 credit" confused Kenneth on sight (2026-11-02), so it is always "1 credit a message", "5 credits a message". Dollars appear only on the page where money changes hands. Plans are Hobby ($10 a month), Workshop ($20 a month) and Pay as you go (the never-expiring pack); never Pro, Plus or Premium.
12	2. **Credits only move when the person sends a message.** Turns the app starts (the file-opened report, the slice-finished note) are free, and the balance never changes without a message from the person. That one fact is what makes the balance trustworthy; it is stated on the pricing page in one sentence: "Only messages you send cost credits."
13	3. **Expiring credits are named by what they are, with a date. Bought credits are just "credits" and never expire.** "First-month credits · 62 of 500 left · Expires 1 Dec." "Free Standard messages · 50 of 50 left · Resets 1 Dec." "Bought credits · 500 left · Never expire." Never a bare number that mixes them. The draw rule is stated once, in the breakdown: "Expiring credits are used first."
14	4. **Say the number before the boundary, not at it.** Every ceiling (balance, fair use, expiry) is shown on the way there with a count, so reaching it is never news.
15	5. **Nothing typed is lost and nothing stops silently.** A message that cannot be sent stays in the composer. (The earlier draft added "with a way to send it anyway"; the design session dropped the phrase on board 0 because a chat now keeps its model, so there is no way to send. That follows from Kenneth's decision but he has not reviewed the wording. The ways forward are to get more credits or, when free Standard messages remain, to start a Standard chat with the typed text carried over.)

96	Back in the app: the balance refreshes when the window regains focus, and the composer shows one line, "+500 credits", so the person knows it worked without opening Preferences.

100	Where: the first launch after day 30.
101	
102	Risk: the person comes back to zero and reads it as "the free trial is over, pay up", the moment Obico's data says people leave. Expert is one click away in the picker (6b) and shows its price. A chat already on Expert stays on Expert, because a chat keeps its model, so opening one shows board 3d.
103	
104	### 10. Rewards for a print report (boards 8a to 8d)
105	
106	Where: Print history, and the project card on Home.
107	
108	Opinion: show the reward before the work, in the button itself: "Tell us how it printed · 25 credits", on the Print history entry beside Print again and Export (8a), absent while printing, one report per G-code. Kenneth pointed at the print-history lesson of 2026-10-27, "don't assume users can easily go back to the original chat and find the card" and "when the print fails, the user is likely in a new chat already", so the chat's one-line G-code marker keeps its "history" link and gets no button. (It worked / Partly / It didn't work), which is the report's outcome, not a print state: Print history stays without a failure state (decided 2026-10-27). Three rewarded reports a day; the form says so only when the person reaches it. Print history has no composer, so the confirmation is the entry's own row, "Report sent · 16:10 · 25 credits added" (8c), which says nothing about how the print went. === liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit
---
name: liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit
description: "RelWithDebInfo liblibslic3r_gui.a crossed Apple ar's 4 GiB archive limit on jusprin-newui (2026-09-13); CMAKE_AR override is ignored; manual llvm-ar relink recipe and its cd trap"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 0771473f-5d46-4419-b8e5-112938ea6b34
  modified: 2026-09-14T14:18:50.456Z
---

On 2026-09-13, at jusprin-newui 770bd2b0a2 (after "Add the evidence-led Add a
printer flow"), a worktree RelWithDebInfo build failed archiving
`src/slic3r/RelWithDebInfo/liblibslic3r_gui.a`:
`Assertion failed: (memberOffset < 0xFFFFFFFF) ... ArchiveWriter.cpp` then
`fatal error in .../ranlib`. The archive llvm-ar produced was 4,309,350,176
bytes; the main checkout's copy built minutes earlier was 4,143,827,796 and
still fit. Objects are big because the root CMakeLists.txt (lines ~544-548)
rewrites RelWithDebInfo -O2 to -O0 on purpose. Disk space was not the cause.

**Why:** the failed build left the OLD harness binary in place, and the harness
runs afterwards "passed" against stale code (a new `--printer-setup` flag
silently ran the default mode: same 285 check count). Gate runs on build
success and compare binary mtime.

**How to apply:**
- `-DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar` on an existing build dir does
  nothing: `CMakeFiles/<ver>/CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake` sets CMAKE_AR as a normal
  variable that shadows the cache.
- Working relink: `ninja -f build-RelWithDebInfo.ninja -t commands <target>`,
  drop compile lines, swap ar/ranlib for llvm-ar/llvm-ranlib on the gui archive
  line only, then run EACH line in its own `(cd build/arm64 && eval "$line")`.
  One `sh` script fails with bogus "no such file" errors because the
  encoding-check line does `cd src/slic3r` and it leaks; `sh -e` also does not
  stop inside `&&` chains. Apple's linker accepted the >4 GiB llvm-ar archive.
- The fix is PER BUILD DIRECTORY, nothing in the repo selects llvm-ar. Main
  checkout's build/arm64 cache has llvm-ar (commit 449b676145 documents it in
  agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md); any newly configured build dir
  gets Apple ar and fails again. Configure new dirs with the flags in
  [[jusprin-worktree-build]].
- Recurred 2026-09-14 on a fresh worktree at jusprin-newui bc19661a7f (archive
  4,308,513,464 bytes). Shortcut that worked: after the failed build, from
  `-t commands shell_integration_harness` drop lines containing ` -c `; only
  the last two remain relevant (gui archive, then harness link). Run just
  those two, swapping ar/ranlib on the archive line. Harness then passed.
- A lasting fix (llvm-ar in the toolchain, thin archives, or less debug info)
  is Kenneth's call; the main checkout will hit this on its next growth.

Related: [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]].
=== check-for-running-ninja-before-nohup-build
---
name: check-for-running-ninja-before-nohup-build
description: "2026-10-21 one idle session left four overlapping nohup Release builds in one build dir, pegging all 12 cores for an hour; pgrep ninja on the build dir before launching, and kill your builds before ending a turn"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: a697178b-3815-42ff-b8cb-a240eb240688
  modified: 2026-10-21T19:02:35.660Z
---

On 2026-10-21 Kenneth's Mac ran at load average 32 on 12 cores for over an hour. The cause was one Claude session (the "Show MCP edits without an agent" worktree session) that launched four `nohup cmake --build … --config Release` runs between 10:56 and 11:05 into the same build dir (`.claude/worktrees/mcp-external-edits/build/arm64`), three with identical target sets. Each ninja spawned ~12 clang jobs, so 56 clang processes fought over 12 cores and every build crawled. The session had gone idle at 11:13 with its work already committed, and the builds kept running as orphans (parent pid 1) because of nohup.

**Why:** a nohup'd build survives the Bash tool timeout (see [[background-bash-timeout-kills-builds]]), so re-launching "the build" after each timeout adds a build instead of resuming one. ninja does not lock the build dir; concurrent instances just duplicate work and thrash.

**How to apply:**
- Before any `nohup cmake --build`, run `pgrep -fl 'ninja -f' ` and `lsof -a -d cwd -p <pid>`; if a ninja already has that build dir as cwd, tail its log instead of starting another.
- Never launch the same target set twice; wait on the saved PID with `kill -0` (see [[pgrep-wait-loop-matches-itself]]).
- Before ending a turn with the task done, kill builds you started that nobody will read (`pkill -P <ninja pid>; kill <ninja pid>`), or say in the recap that one is still running and why.
- To find who owns a stray build: the ninja's stdout path (`lsof -p <pid> -d 1`) contains the Claude Code session id; `ps -o args= -p $(pgrep -f -- "--resume=<id>")` shows the app session's side-session-notes path.

---
name: cmake-file-edit-forces-full-rebuild
description: "Editing sources.cmake (adding a file) after a commit re-runs CMake, which bakes the new HEAD into -DGIT_COMMIT_HASH on every compile line, so ninja rebuilds all ~970 steps."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 62f57a5d-138a-485a-ac71-94d683a8c5db
  modified: 2026-11-01T13:16:25.404Z
---

2026-10-24 (import-behavior work, PR TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin#38): adding EmptyPlateHint.cpp to `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/sources.cmake` after committing made the next build re-run CMake. The configure step reads the git hash into `-DGIT_COMMIT_HASH=\"<sha>\"`, which is on every TU's command line, so the whole tree (libslic3r included) recompiled at -j4: roughly an hour.

Not the only cause of that symptom: if the build log starts with "premature end of file; recovering", see [[ninja-deps-bad-record-repeat-rebuild]].

**Why:** a command-line change invalidates every object in ninja's log, not just the touched target.
**How to apply:** add new source files to `sources.cmake` before the first build of a worktree, and avoid committing between a cmake-file edit and the build that needs it. Related: [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[pkill-cmake-build-leaves-ninja]].

Also learned that day: OrcaSlicer reinstalls its own `PlaterDropTarget` after every slice completes (`Plater::priv::on_process_completed`, `is_finished` is true for every non-slice-all run), so any fork-owned Plater drop target must be put back afterwards (the shell does it on idle).

Author: Kenneth Jiang <kenneth.jiang@gmail.com>
Date:   Tue Oct 6 18:47:26 2026 -0700

    Add the local first-run onboarding flow to Home
    
    A new user now gets a short guided path into a first project instead of
    landing on an empty Home screen. The path needs no account and no Agent:
    welcome, import presets from an existing OrcaSlicer install, confirm or
    choose a printer setup, then open a project or the bundled example.
    
    How it works
    - The native side decides which step is due. OnboardingModel is a pure
      function from saved progress plus three facts (user presets exist, a
      usable printer is selected, a project is open) to the next step.
      OrcaHomeBackend supplies the facts and stores progress in the app
      config under "jusprin_onboarding".
    - The Home page draws the step it is told to draw (Onboarding.tsx). The
      eight screens follow the Figma frames on the "On boarding experience"
      page; at 1280x800 the main block of each lands on its frame's
      rectangle.
    - The Home bridge stays on protocol version 1. The new state and
      messages are additive and announced through an "onboarding" entry in
      the capabilities list.
    
    What the page shows is what the app reported
    - The Figma frames carry sample data (an example source, example preset
      rows, a sample failure reason). None of it is repeated: preset names,
      counts, and the copied and not-copied lists come from the host, and a
      line the host cannot back is left out.
    - The three preset-kind checkboxes control what is imported, and
      "Review selection" lists the preset names found in the Orca folder.
    - A failed action is reported: on the project step as the recovery
      card, where Retry repeats the action that failed, and on other steps
      as a line above the buttons.
    
    Deliberately not built
    - Account and Agent setup. "Set up JusPrin" and "Set up with Agent" are
      links that open jusprin.com/account.
    - The four dropdowns on the setup confirmation show the current value

    Add the local first-run onboarding flow to Home
    
    A new user now gets a short guided path into a first project instead of
    landing on an empty Home screen. The path needs no account and no Agent:
    welcome, import presets from an existing OrcaSlicer install, confirm or
    choose a printer setup, then open a project or the bundled example.
    
    How it works
    - The native side decides which step is due. OnboardingModel is a pure
      function from saved progress plus three facts (user presets exist, a
      usable printer is selected, a project is open) to the next step.
      OrcaHomeBackend supplies the facts and stores progress in the app
      config under "jusprin_onboarding".
    - The Home page draws the step it is told to draw (Onboarding.tsx). The
      eight screens follow the Figma frames on the "On boarding experience"
      page; at 1280x800 the main block of each lands on its frame's
      rectangle.
    - The Home bridge stays on protocol version 1. The new state and
      messages are additive and announced through an "onboarding" entry in
      the capabilities list.
    
    What the page shows is what the app reported
    - The Figma frames carry sample data (an example source, example preset
      rows, a sample failure reason). None of it is repeated: preset names,
      counts, and the copied and not-copied lists come from the host, and a
      line the host cannot back is left out.
    - The three preset-kind checkboxes control what is imported, and
      "Review selection" lists the preset names found in the Orca folder.
    - A failed action is reported: on the project step as the recovery
      card, where Retry repeats the action that failed, and on other steps
      as a line above the buttons.
    
    Deliberately not built
    - Account and Agent setup. "Set up JusPrin" and "Set up with Agent" are
      links that open jusprin.com/account.
    - The four dropdowns on the setup confirmation show the current value
      only; changing one goes through "Change or find printer".
    - Two sizes follow the token file where Figma differs: the close button
      is 26 px (Figma 32) and the breadcrumb chevron 16 px (Figma 14).

    480, example panel 472, setup field 220), guarded in
    test_brand_tokens.cpp. Home now also emits the checkbox, select, and
    form-row tokens as CSS variables.
    
    Verified: Home page tests (70), jusprin_tests (584 assertions), and
    brand_tokens_tests pass. Every screen was captured from the built app on
    isolated data folders and compared with Figma.
    
    Not verified end to end: a real import that leaves some presets behind
    (the partial-result screen was shown from a stored result), and the
    change that keeps the user on Home when the bundled example fails to
    open. The failure was reproduced before the change; the corrected
    behaviour was not demonstrated.

Author: Kenneth Jiang <kenneth.jiang@gmail.com>
Date:   Tue Oct 6 18:47:26 2026 -0700

    Add the local first-run onboarding flow to Home
    
    A new user now gets a short guided path into a first project instead of
    landing on an empty Home screen. The path needs no account and no Agent:
    welcome, import presets from an existing OrcaSlicer install, confirm or
    choose a printer setup, then open a project or the bundled example.
    
    How it works
    - The native side decides which step is due. OnboardingModel is a pure
      function from saved progress plus three facts (user presets exist, a
      usable printer is selected, a project is open) to the next step.
      OrcaHomeBackend supplies the facts and stores progress in the app
      config under "jusprin_onboarding".
    - The Home page draws the step it is told to draw (Onboarding.tsx). The
      eight screens follow the Figma frames on the "On boarding experience"
      page; at 1280x800 the main block of each lands on its frame's
      rectangle.
    - The Home bridge stays on protocol version 1. The new state and
      messages are additive and announced through an "onboarding" entry in
      the capabilities list.
    
    What the page shows is what the app reported
    - The Figma frames carry sample data (an example source, example preset
      rows, a sample failure reason). None of it is repeated: preset names,
      counts, and the copied and not-copied lists come from the host, and a
      line the host cannot back is left out.
    - The three preset-kind checkboxes control what is imported, and
      "Review selection" lists the preset names found in the Orca folder.
    - A failed action is reported: on the project step as the recovery
      card, where Retry repeats the action that failed, and on other steps
      as a line above the buttons.
    
    Deliberately not built
    - Account and Agent setup. "Set up JusPrin" and "Set up with Agent" are
      links that open jusprin.com/account.
    - The four dropdowns on the setup confirmation show the current value
      only; changing one goes through "Change or find printer".
    - Two sizes follow the token file where Figma differs: the close button
      is 26 px (Figma 32) and the breadcrumb chevron 16 px (Figma 14).
    
    Tokens: component.onboarding gains the frame widths (content 960, card
    480, example panel 472, setup field 220), guarded in
    test_brand_tokens.cpp. Home now also emits the checkbox, select, and
    form-row tokens as CSS variables.
    
    Verified: Home page tests (70), jusprin_tests (584 assertions), and
    brand_tokens_tests pass. Every screen was captured from the built app on
    isolated data folders and compared with Figma.
    
    Not verified end to end: a real import that leaves some presets behind
    (the partial-result screen was shown from a stored result), and the
    change that keeps the user on Home when the bundled example fails to
    open. The failure was reproduced before the change; the corrected
    behaviour was not demonstrated.

172	
173	On 2026-10-21 Kenneth's Mac ran at load average 32 on 12 cores for over an hour. The cause was one Claude session (the "Show MCP edits without an agent" worktree session) that launched four `nohup cmake --build … --config Release` runs between 10:56 and 11:05 into the same build dir (`.claude/worktrees/mcp-external-edits/build/arm64`), three with identical target sets. Each ninja spawned ~12 clang jobs, so 56 clang processes fought over 12 cores and every build crawled. The session had gone idle at 11:13 with its work already committed, and the builds kept running as orphans (parent pid 1) because of nohup.
174	
175	**Why:** a nohup'd build survives the Bash tool timeout (see [[background-bash-timeout-kills-builds]]), so re-launching "the build" after each timeout adds a build instead of resuming one. ninja does not lock the build dir; concurrent instances just duplicate work and thrash.
176	
177	**How to apply:**
178	- Before any `nohup cmake --build`, run `pgrep -fl 'ninja -f' ` and `lsof -a -d cwd -p <pid>`; if a ninja already has that build dir as cwd, tail its log instead of starting another.
179	- Never launch the same target set twice; wait on the saved PID with `kill -0` (see [[pgrep-wait-loop-matches-itself]]).
180	- Before ending a turn with the task done, kill builds you started that nobody will read (`pkill -P <ninja pid>; kill <ninja pid>`), or say in the recap that one is still running and why.

372	On 2026-10-28 I walked six scenarios (open-and-print, fix-a-problem) through the real app with Opus 5.5 and published the critique at https://claude.ai/artifact/XyVvteGiKhiJ6apUx8rcmR (34 frames, scratch copy at scratchpad/ux/ of that session). Kenneth's steer: start from files people actually download (MakerWorld 3MFs carry a full Bambu profile: printer, print preset, filaments, colours, bed type, designer, licence), not from generated STLs. `~/Downloads` has Tape_4_3MF.3mf (A1 mini profile), find_my_hollow.3mf (P1S, 3 colours, 233 mm wide, too big for an A1 mini), arrow_headband.3mf (P1S), general_purpose_hook.STL (bare).
373	
374	**Recipe that worked**
375	- `ditto` the built .app out of `build/arm64/src/RelWithDebInfo/` into the scratchpad before launching (another session's ninja can relink it underneath you); the bundle id is already unique (`io.jusprin.JusPrin`), no re-sign needed.
376	- `ditto` `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2` to a scratch `--datadir`; set `jusprin.fake_printer=true`, `presets.machine` to the saved "Bambu Lab A1 mini 2", write `jusprin/fake_printer.json`, delete `jusprin/mcp.json.lock`.
377	- **Clear `local_machines`.** Kenneth's conf carries a `local_machines` entry keyed by the empty string (old Moonraker experiment). With the fake Bambu agent on, `init_networking_callbacks`' connect callback calls `DeviceManager::set_selected_machine("")` in a loop ("same lan machine, dev_id =, disconnect and reconnect"), the main window disappears and the log grew 700 MB in two minutes. Clearing the map fixed it. The loop has no guard; see [[fake-bambu-printer-sim]] and [[harness-fake-printer-cleanup]].
378	- Background `app_*` tools cannot press OrcaSlicer's custom `Button`s (no AX action) and the hit test at the dialog's screen position reports "belongs to a different process". `request_full_control` + `computer_batch` works for everything, including the Agent web view and the macOS file chooser (`cmd+shift+g`, type the path, Return, Return). Re-front the app with `open_application` when another session's harness steals focus.
379	- Every `app_screenshot`/`computer_batch` screenshot is written as a JPEG under `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>/tool-results/mcp-computer-use-blob-*.jpg`; copy those for a report instead of fighting `screencapture`.
380	- The dev build (-O0) slices a 38 mm part in over a minute; wait 45–60 s before judging a slice.
381	
382	**Why:** the first launch attempt looked like an app bug (blank window, title "Couldn't save") and cost ten minutes; the dialog-click refusals cost another ten.

384	=== live-test-built-app-on-mac
385	---
386	name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
387	description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
388	metadata: 
389	  node_type: memory
390	  type: project
391	  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
392	  modified: 2026-11-01T19:29:08.107Z
393	---
394	
395	Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.
396	
397	**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.
398	
399	The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.
400	
401	**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.
402	
403	**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].
404	
405	**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
406	2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
407	`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
408	`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
409	app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
410	a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
411	on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
412	the harness had opened on the Acer.
413	
414	Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
415	(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
416	captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
417	not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
418	"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.
419	
420	The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
421	read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
422	and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
423	evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
424	being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
425	concluding anything about the app.
426	
427	**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
428	`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
429	(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
430	`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
431	the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.
432	
433	**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
434	`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
435	`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
436	all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
437	directory — the directory alone is not enough.
438	
439	**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.
440	
441	**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.
442	
443	**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.
444	
445	**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
446	against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
447	first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
448	agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
449	had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
450	`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
451	all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
452	treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
453	`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
454	rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.
455	
456	**2026-09-19 addendum:** background `app_click` on the Home/Agent WKWebViews reports
457	"ok … unverified" and nothing happens; only display-scope `computer_batch` clicks
458	reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the
459	display tools default to the Acer, so `switch_display` first. `Return` in the composer
460	sends in the real app; in the built-in-browser fixture it does not (click the send
461	button). Another Claude session holding the computer-use lock blocks `request_access`
462	until Kenneth stops that session. Page-only states are cheaper via [[fake-host-page-fixture]].
463	
464	**2026-10-28: background clicks no longer open header popups.** In `--manual`, background `app_click` on the printer chip (body or chevron) left the chip pressed but no menu appeared, and `--printer-menu-capture`'s screen blit came back solid black with the screen unlocked (likely a rebuilt binary losing screen-recording permission). For header menu rows, use `HeaderButton::snapshot(2.0)` in the harness instead (see `ring_dashes` in `capture_chip_appearance`).
465	
466	**Modal dialogs ignore synthetic input (2026-10-28).** OrcaSlicer's own modal dialogs (Send print job, Previously opened file) took no click or key from computer-use in either mode: background app_click is refused ("belongs to a different process") and display clicks/keys do nothing, though log/AX showed the dialog topmost and the app idle. Kenneth's real click on Send worked at once. Web-view screens (Home cards) and menu shortcuts (Cmd+R slice, Cmd+Shift+G send dialog) do work. So when a step needs a modal's button, ask Kenneth to press it and watch the log; don't spend turns on monitors or overlays. Also: launch the copy with `open -n <copy>.app --args --datadir …`, never the binary from the shell (that instance took no input at all), and trim the datadir's `recent_projects` to non-Downloads paths or startup stalls on a macOS Downloads-access prompt.
467	
468	**Header popups and Open dialogs (2026-11-01).** A background `app_click` on a chip half opens its popup only while the app is frontmost: set frontmost with System Events by unix id, click, find the popup's id with a `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` lister (layer 101), then `app_screenshot` that raw id. File > Open's panel belongs to another process, and computer-use refuses input to it and says not to work around that; open the file with the MCP `project_open` tool instead (`load_project(path, "<loadall>")`, against File > Open's `"-"`) and say so. lldb on the RelWithDebInfo build reads and forces flags without touching code: `(Slic3r::GUI::GUI_App*)wxApp::ms_appInstance`, then `preset_bundle->printers.m_edited_preset`; read the Print's flags with a breakpoint on `Print::validate`, because `plater_->p->fff_print` still holds default settings.
469	=== background-bash-timeout-kills-builds
470	---
471	name: background-bash-timeout-kills-builds
472	description: "A run_in_background Bash build dies at the tool timeout (ninja prints \"interrupted by user\", exit 130); launch long builds with nohup and watch the log instead"
473	metadata: 
474	  node_type: memory
475	  type: feedback
476	  originSessionId: 8c1e8dd3-1475-48e9-9398-2d5eaa424bab
477	  modified: 2026-09-14T19:01:34.576Z
478	---
479	
480	A `cmake --build` started with the Bash tool's `run_in_background` is still
481	bound by that call's `timeout` (default 120 s, max 600 s). When it fires the
482	build log ends with `ninja: build stopped: interrupted by user.` and `exit=130`,
483	which looks like a human Ctrl-C but is the harness. Seen 2026-09-14 on a
484	725-step JusPrin rebuild.
485	
486	**Why:** the notification says "completed" and the log shows no compiler
487	error, so it is easy to misread as a finished build; the changed files had not
488	compiled at all.
489	
490	**How to apply:** for anything longer than a few minutes, start it detached
491	(`nohup sh -c "cmake --build … > log 2>&1; echo exit=\$? >> log" & disown`),
492	then arm a Monitor on the log that reports progress and the `exit=` line. Check
493	`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' log` before trusting the result. Related:
494	[[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]], [[jusprin-worktree-build]].
495	=== reproduce-on-real-app-not-fakes
496	---
497	name: reproduce-on-real-app-not-fakes
498	description: "A failing test with a fake backend is not a reproduction; run the pre-fix code against the real thing before fixing, and say what was and was not seen"
499	metadata:
500	  type: feedback
501	---
502	
503	A failing Catch2 test with a fake backend proves the code does what the brief says, not that the bug is real. Before fixing, run the code from before the fix against the real thing, with what the app actually knows printed beside what it says.
504	
505	**Why:** on 2026-11-01 Kenneth asked whether I had reproduced three printer chat bugs, and I had only fakes for them: "I don't want you to fix the bugs that are in imagination only". The real run then showed one was only partly real as briefed: the "No printer in LAN mode" sentence was true of a printer in cloud mode.
506	
507	**How to apply:** do it before writing the fix. To do it afterwards, swap production files with `git show <base>:<file>`, keep a temporary harness script, rebuild, and restore from `git show HEAD:<file>`. In zsh, loop over an array: a plain string variable does not split. Run harnesses with cwd in the scratchpad: the Bambu plug-in writes `log_iotc.txt` into the cwd. See [[printer-network-check-harness]].
508	=== prove-guard-tests-fail-first
509	---
510	name: prove-guard-tests-fail-first
511	description: A lint-style test that reads a source file must be shown failing on injected drift before it counts; Vitest hands CSS imports (even ?raw) back empty in the AgentUI setup.
512	metadata: 
513	  node_type: memory
514	  type: feedback
515	  originSessionId: 1b302f25-67a5-44d7-9f2c-02b68b2a0bb8
516	  modified: 2026-09-07T23:29:44.393Z
517	---
518	
519	In `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI`, `import css from './styles.css?raw'` under Vitest resolves to an empty string, and `new URL('./x', import.meta.url)` is not a `file:` URL in the jsdom environment. A stylesheet-guard test written either way passed green while asserting nothing.
520	
521	**Why:** Vitest's CSS handling short-circuits the import before Vite's `?raw` asset path runs, so every regex over the "stylesheet" matched nothing. Only appending a deliberate `border-radius: 4px` to the file and watching the suite stay green exposed it.
522	
523	**How to apply:** Read source files in tests with `readFileSync(join(__dirname, ...))` and assert the text is non-empty. For any guard test that scans a file, inject the violation it exists to catch, confirm it fails naming the offender, then restore. Related: [[render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof]], [[fork-rebase-risk-verify-before-claiming]].

=== jusprin-worktree-build
---
name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).

=== liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit
---
name: liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit
description: "RelWithDebInfo liblibslic3r_gui.a crossed Apple ar's 4 GiB archive limit on jusprin-newui (2026-09-13); CMAKE_AR override is ignored; manual llvm-ar relink recipe and its cd trap"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 0771473f-5d46-4419-b8e5-112938ea6b34
  modified: 2026-09-14T14:18:50.456Z
---

On 2026-09-13, at jusprin-newui 770bd2b0a2 (after "Add the evidence-led Add a
printer flow"), a worktree RelWithDebInfo build failed archiving
`src/slic3r/RelWithDebInfo/liblibslic3r_gui.a`:
`Assertion failed: (memberOffset < 0xFFFFFFFF) ... ArchiveWriter.cpp` then
`fatal error in .../ranlib`. The archive llvm-ar produced was 4,309,350,176
bytes; the main checkout's copy built minutes earlier was 4,143,827,796 and
still fit. Objects are big because the root CMakeLists.txt (lines ~544-548)
rewrites RelWithDebInfo -O2 to -O0 on purpose. Disk space was not the cause.

**Why:** the failed build left the OLD harness binary in place, and the harness
runs afterwards "passed" against stale code (a new `--printer-setup` flag
silently ran the default mode: same 285 check count). Gate runs on build
success and compare binary mtime.

**How to apply:**
- `-DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar` on an existing build dir does
  nothing: `CMakeFiles/<ver>/CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake` sets CMAKE_AR as a normal
  variable that shadows the cache.
- Working relink: `ninja -f build-RelWithDebInfo.ninja -t commands <target>`,
  drop compile lines, swap ar/ranlib for llvm-ar/llvm-ranlib on the gui archive
  line only, then run EACH line in its own `(cd build/arm64 && eval "$line")`.
  One `sh` script fails with bogus "no such file" errors because the
  encoding-check line does `cd src/slic3r` and it leaks; `sh -e` also does not
  stop inside `&&` chains. Apple's linker accepted the >4 GiB llvm-ar archive.
- The fix is PER BUILD DIRECTORY, nothing in the repo selects llvm-ar. Main
  checkout's build/arm64 cache has llvm-ar (commit 449b676145 documents it in
  agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md); any newly configured build dir
  gets Apple ar and fails again. Configure new dirs with the flags in
  [[jusprin-worktree-build]].
- Recurred 2026-09-14 on a fresh worktree at jusprin-newui bc19661a7f (archive
  4,308,513,464 bytes). Shortcut that worked: after the failed build, from
  `-t commands shell_integration_harness` drop lines containing ` -c `; only
  the last two remain relevant (gui archive, then harness link). Run just
  those two, swapping ar/ranlib on the archive line. Harness then passed.
- A lasting fix (llvm-ar in the toolchain, thin archives, or less debug info)
  is Kenneth's call; the main checkout will hit this on its next growth.

Related: [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]].
=== check-for-running-ninja-before-nohup-build
---
name: check-for-running-ninja-before-nohup-build
description: "2026-10-21 one idle session left four overlapping nohup Release builds in one build dir, pegging all 12 cores for an hour; pgrep ninja on the build dir before launching, and kill your builds before ending a turn"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: a697178b-3815-42ff-b8cb-a240eb240688
  modified: 2026-10-21T19:02:35.660Z
---

On 2026-10-21 Kenneth's Mac ran at load average 32 on 12 cores for over an hour. The cause was one Claude session (the "Show MCP edits without an agent" worktree session) that launched four `nohup cmake --build … --config Release` runs between 10:56 and 11:05 into the same build dir (`.claude/worktrees/mcp-external-edits/build/arm64`), three with identical target sets. Each ninja spawned ~12 clang jobs, so 56 clang processes fought over 12 cores and every build crawled. The session had gone idle at 11:13 with its work already committed, and the builds kept running as orphans (parent pid 1) because of nohup.

**Why:** a nohup'd build survives the Bash tool timeout (see [[background-bash-timeout-kills-builds]]), so re-launching "the build" after each timeout adds a build instead of resuming one. ninja does not lock the build dir; concurrent instances just duplicate work and thrash.

**How to apply:**
- Before any `nohup cmake --build`, run `pgrep -fl 'ninja -f' ` and `lsof -a -d cwd -p <pid>`; if a ninja already has that build dir as cwd, tail its log instead of starting another.
- Never launch the same target set twice; wait on the saved PID with `kill -0` (see [[pgrep-wait-loop-matches-itself]]).
- Before ending a turn with the task done, kill builds you started that nobody will read (`pkill -P <ninja pid>; kill <ninja pid>`), or say in the recap that one is still running and why.
- To find who owns a stray build: the ninja's stdout path (`lsof -p <pid> -d 1`) contains the Claude Code session id; `ps -o args= -p $(pgrep -f -- "--resume=<id>")` shows the app session's side-session-notes path.
=== cmake-file-edit-forces-full-rebuild
---
name: cmake-file-edit-forces-full-rebuild
description: "Editing sources.cmake (adding a file) after a commit re-runs CMake, which bakes the new HEAD into -DGIT_COMMIT_HASH on every compile line, so ninja rebuilds all ~970 steps."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 62f57a5d-138a-485a-ac71-94d683a8c5db
  modified: 2026-11-01T13:16:25.404Z
---

2026-10-24 (import-behavior work, PR TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin#38): adding EmptyPlateHint.cpp to `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/sources.cmake` after committing made the next build re-run CMake. The configure step reads the git hash into `-DGIT_COMMIT_HASH=\"<sha>\"`, which is on every TU's command line, so the whole tree (libslic3r included) recompiled at -j4: roughly an hour.

Not the only cause of that symptom: if the build log starts with "premature end of file; recovering", see [[ninja-deps-bad-record-repeat-rebuild]].

**Why:** a command-line change invalidates every object in ninja's log, not just the touched target.
**How to apply:** add new source files to `sources.cmake` before the first build of a worktree, and avoid committing between a cmake-file edit and the build that needs it. Related: [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[pkill-cmake-build-leaves-ninja]].

Also learned that day: OrcaSlicer reinstalls its own `PlaterDropTarget` after every slice completes (`Plater::priv::on_process_completed`, `is_finished` is true for every non-slice-all run), so any fork-owned Plater drop target must be put back afterwards (the shell does it on idle).

On 2026-10-28 I walked six scenarios (open-and-print, fix-a-problem) through the real app with Opus 5.5 and published the critique at https://claude.ai/artifact/XyVvteGiKhiJ6apUx8rcmR (34 frames, scratch copy at scratchpad/ux/ of that session). Kenneth's steer: start from files people actually download (MakerWorld 3MFs carry a full Bambu profile: printer, print preset, filaments, colours, bed type, designer, licence), not from generated STLs. `~/Downloads` has Tape_4_3MF.3mf (A1 mini profile), find_my_hollow.3mf (P1S, 3 colours, 233 mm wide, too big for an A1 mini), arrow_headband.3mf (P1S), general_purpose_hook.STL (bare).

**Recipe that worked**
- `ditto` the built .app out of `build/arm64/src/RelWithDebInfo/` into the scratchpad before launching (another session's ninja can relink it underneath you); the bundle id is already unique (`io.jusprin.JusPrin`), no re-sign needed.

- **Clear `local_machines`.** Kenneth's conf carries a `local_machines` entry keyed by the empty string (old Moonraker experiment). With the fake Bambu agent on, `init_networking_callbacks`' connect callback calls `DeviceManager::set_selected_machine("")` in a loop ("same lan machine, dev_id =, disconnect and reconnect"), the main window disappears and the log grew 700 MB in two minutes. Clearing the map fixed it. The loop has no guard; see [[fake-bambu-printer-sim]] and [[harness-fake-printer-cleanup]].
- Background `app_*` tools cannot press OrcaSlicer's custom `Button`s (no AX action) and the hit test at the dialog's screen position reports "belongs to a different process". `request_full_control` + `computer_batch` works for everything, including the Agent web view and the macOS file chooser (`cmd+shift+g`, type the path, Return, Return). Re-front the app with `open_application` when another session's harness steals focus.
- Every `app_screenshot`/`computer_batch` screenshot is written as a JPEG under `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>/tool-results/mcp-computer-use-blob-*.jpg`; copy those for a report instead of fighting `screencapture`.
- The dev build (-O0) slices a 38 mm part in over a minute; wait 45–60 s before judging a slice.

**Why:** the first launch attempt looked like an app bug (blank window, title "Couldn't save") and cost ten minutes; the dialog-click refusals cost another ten.
**How to apply:** reuse this for any "walk through the app as a user" request; keep scenarios on downloaded files; write the critique per step as what the person knows / sees / finds confusing. Related: [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[drive-app-with-posted-key-events]].
=== live-test-built-app-on-mac
---
name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-11-01T19:29:08.107Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

**2026-09-19 addendum:** background `app_click` on the Home/Agent WKWebViews reports
"ok … unverified" and nothing happens; only display-scope `computer_batch` clicks
reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the
display tools default to the Acer, so `switch_display` first. `Return` in the composer
sends in the real app; in the built-in-browser fixture it does not (click the send
button). Another Claude session holding the computer-use lock blocks `request_access`
until Kenneth stops that session. Page-only states are cheaper via [[fake-host-page-fixture]].

**2026-10-28: background clicks no longer open header popups.** In `--manual`, background `app_click` on the printer chip (body or chevron) left the chip pressed but no menu appeared, and `--printer-menu-capture`'s screen blit came back solid black with the screen unlocked (likely a rebuilt binary losing screen-recording permission). For header menu rows, use `HeaderButton::snapshot(2.0)` in the harness instead (see `ring_dashes` in `capture_chip_appearance`).

**Modal dialogs ignore synthetic input (2026-10-28).** OrcaSlicer's own modal dialogs (Send print job, Previously opened file) took no click or key from computer-use in either mode: background app_click is refused ("belongs to a different process") and display clicks/keys do nothing, though log/AX showed the dialog topmost and the app idle. Kenneth's real click on Send worked at once. Web-view screens (Home cards) and menu shortcuts (Cmd+R slice, Cmd+Shift+G send dialog) do work. So when a step needs a modal's button, ask Kenneth to press it and watch the log; don't spend turns on monitors or overlays. Also: launch the copy with `open -n <copy>.app --args --datadir …`, never the binary from the shell (that instance took no input at all), and trim the datadir's `recent_projects` to non-Downloads paths or startup stalls on a macOS Downloads-access prompt.

**Header popups and Open dialogs (2026-11-01).** A background `app_click` on a chip half opens its popup only while the app is frontmost: set frontmost with System Events by unix id, click, find the popup's id with a `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` lister (layer 101), then `app_screenshot` that raw id. File > Open's panel belongs to another process, and computer-use refuses input to it and says not to work around that; open the file with the MCP `project_open` tool instead (`load_project(path, "<loadall>")`, against File > Open's `"-"`) and say so. lldb on the RelWithDebInfo build reads and forces flags without touching code: `(Slic3r::GUI::GUI_App*)wxApp::ms_appInstance`, then `preset_bundle->printers.m_edited_preset`; read the Print's flags with a breakpoint on `Print::validate`, because `plater_->p->fff_print` still holds default settings.
=== background-bash-timeout-kills-builds
---
name: background-bash-timeout-kills-builds
description: "A run_in_background Bash build dies at the tool timeout (ninja prints \"interrupted by user\", exit 130); launch long builds with nohup and watch the log instead"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 8c1e8dd3-1475-48e9-9398-2d5eaa424bab
  modified: 2026-09-14T19:01:34.576Z
---

A `cmake --build` started with the Bash tool's `run_in_background` is still
bound by that call's `timeout` (default 120 s, max 600 s). When it fires the
build log ends with `ninja: build stopped: interrupted by user.` and `exit=130`,
which looks like a human Ctrl-C but is the harness. Seen 2026-09-14 on a
725-step JusPrin rebuild.

**Why:** the notification says "completed" and the log shows no compiler
error, so it is easy to misread as a finished build; the changed files had not
compiled at all.

**How to apply:** for anything longer than a few minutes, start it detached
(`nohup sh -c "cmake --build … > log 2>&1; echo exit=\$? >> log" & disown`),
then arm a Monitor on the log that reports progress and the `exit=` line. Check
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' log` before trusting the result. Related:
[[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]], [[jusprin-worktree-build]].
=== reproduce-on-real-app-not-fakes
---
name: reproduce-on-real-app-not-fakes
description: "A failing test with a fake backend is not a reproduction; run the pre-fix code against the real thing before fixing, and say what was and was not seen"
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

A failing Catch2 test with a fake backend proves the code does what the brief says, not that the bug is real. Before fixing, run the code from before the fix against the real thing, with what the app actually knows printed beside what it says.

**Why:** on 2026-11-01 Kenneth asked whether I had reproduced three printer chat bugs, and I had only fakes for them: "I don't want you to fix the bugs that are in imagination only". The real run then showed one was only partly real as briefed: the "No printer in LAN mode" sentence was true of a printer in cloud mode.

**How to apply:** do it before writing the fix. To do it afterwards, swap production files with `git show <base>:<file>`, keep a temporary harness script, rebuild, and restore from `git show HEAD:<file>`. In zsh, loop over an array: a plain string variable does not split. Run harnesses with cwd in the scratchpad: the Bambu plug-in writes `log_iotc.txt` into the cwd. See [[printer-network-check-harness]].
=== prove-guard-tests-fail-first
---
name: prove-guard-tests-fail-first
description: A lint-style test that reads a source file must be shown failing on injected drift before it counts; Vitest hands CSS imports (even ?raw) back empty in the AgentUI setup.
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 1b302f25-67a5-44d7-9f2c-02b68b2a0bb8
  modified: 2026-09-07T23:29:44.393Z
---

In `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI`, `import css from './styles.css?raw'` under Vitest resolves to an empty string, and `new URL('./x', import.meta.url)` is not a `file:` URL in the jsdom environment. A stylesheet-guard test written either way passed green while asserting nothing.

**Why:** Vitest's CSS handling short-circuits the import before Vite's `?raw` asset path runs, so every regex over the "stylesheet" matched nothing. Only appending a deliberate `border-radius: 4px` to the file and watching the suite stay green exposed it.

**How to apply:** Read source files in tests with `readFileSync(join(__dirname, ...))` and assert the text is non-empty. For any guard test that scans a file, inject the violation it exists to catch, confirm it fails naming the offender, then restore. Related: [[render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof]], [[fork-rebase-risk-verify-before-claiming]].

1	# Fork stewardship
2	
3	**Status:** Required discipline for every change to an upstream-owned file on `jusprin-newui`.
4	
5	JusPrin is a long-lived fork. Every line it changes in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line it re-resolves at every rebase, forever, by a person who was not there when the line was written. The rules below exist to keep that permanent cost small and, where it cannot be small, to keep it visible.
6	
7	One question generates all of them: **after this change, what does the fork own?**
8	
9	- Owning *product policy* is safe. It is ours, upstream will never write it, and it lives in our files.
10	- Owning a *small neutral seam* is acceptable. It is the kind of thing upstream might plausibly have written itself, so it survives refactors and could be contributed back.
11	- Owning *upstream's behavior* is the expensive kind. It commits us to re-deriving upstream's intent forever, and the day we take ownership is usually the day the behavior quietly diverges.
12	
13	Two mechanical facts drive everything else. Git merges text, not meaning: it conflicts when two sides touch the same or adjacent lines, and it stays silent when they touch different lines even if the result is nonsense. And a conflict is a *stop* — a human is forced to look — while silent divergence is unbounded and invisible. Conflicts are therefore not the enemy. Unnoticed drift is, and conflicts that resolve wrongly are.
14	
15	## The ten principles
16	
17	### 1. Conflict probability is about where you write, not how much
18	
19	**Rule.** Place fork edits where upstream rarely writes, and keep the number of distinct sites low.
20	
21	**Mechanism.** Risk is roughly *how often upstream edits this region* times *how much of the region you occupy*, summed over every place you touched. Each site is an independent draw. New files have probability zero, so their size is free; one line inside a function upstream is actively reworking is expensive.
22	
23	**The test.** How many separate places does this change touch, and how busy is each one? Would one seam deliver the same capability?
24	
25	**Violation.** Delivering a single capability through a dozen scattered notification lines across several upstream files, when one funnel that every path already passes through would have carried them.
26	
27	### 2. A clean merge is not a safe merge
28	
29	**Rule.** Prefer edits that are locally correct over edits that participate in upstream's control flow.
30	
31	**Mechanism.** Git merges text. If your edit's correctness depends on the code around it — an ordering, a guard, an early return, an invariant nobody wrote down — upstream can restructure the surroundings, the merge succeeds, and your edit now runs under assumptions that no longer hold, with no signal at all.
32	
33	**The test.** If upstream restructures the code around this hunk, do I get a conflict or silence? If silence, would any test catch it?
34	
35	**Violation.** Moving a member out of a constructor's initializer list because a callback can fire mid-construction. Nothing in upstream's code records that invariant, so a future cleanup restores the old form with no conflict and no error.
36	
37	### 3. Add to upstream's code; do not revise it
38	
39	**Rule.** Append, insert, and call. Do not rewrite upstream functions or change their signatures.
40	
41	**Mechanism.** An additive hook fails gracefully: when it conflicts, the resolution is "keep both," and anyone can do that correctly. A rewritten function fails badly: every future upstream change to it is a conflict whose resolution requires re-deriving two intents at once, in code no longer shared with upstream. Rewriting subtle logic also tends to change it, and you find out later.
42	
43	**The test.** Does upstream's line survive my change? If I deleted or replaced one, why could I not have added next to it?
44	
45	**Violation.** Replacing OrcaSlicer's undo and redo implementations with fork-owned equivalents in order to learn whether the history position moved. Re-expressing the vendor-specific snapshot walk silently dropped one of its branches. An additive helper that reports the result, leaving upstream's functions untouched, would have answered the same question.
46	
47	### 4. Own the policy; borrow the mechanism
48	
49	**Rule.** No product name, color, dimension, or product-specific decision in an upstream-owned file. Upstream files may gain small neutral capabilities; the policy that uses them lives in fork-owned code.
50	
51	**Mechanism.** Product specifics in upstream files are permanent divergence: they can never be upstreamed and never dropped, so they must be re-resolved forever. A neutral capability — a flag, a getter/setter pair, an event — reads like something upstream could have written, which is exactly why it survives refactors.
52	
53	**The test.** Would this addition look reasonable in an upstream pull request, with no explanation of our product?
54	
55	**Violation.** A product-named enum value inside a rendering class, or product decisions embedded in an upstream mouse handler. The fix is a neutral options struct plus a fork-owned controller that applies our policy.
56	
57	### 5. One seam beats many touch points
58	
59	**Rule.** Find the single place every path already passes through, and put the fork's line there.
60	
61	**Mechanism.** Each touch point is an independent conflict draw and an independent thing a future resolver must understand. Collapsing many small recurring costs into one is worth some indirection.
62	
63	**The test.** Do all the paths I am hooking already converge somewhere downstream? Is there one function that runs exactly when the thing I care about has happened?
64	
65	**Violation.** Publishing a history-changed event from undo, from redo, and from both history-navigation entry points, when all four funnel through a single update function that runs only on a successful move.
66	
67	### 6. One shared implementation is worth a guaranteed conflict
68	
69	**Rule.** When the alternative is two copies of the same behavior, keep the shared path and accept that it will conflict.
70	
71	**Mechanism.** A conflict is a stop; drift between two copies is silent and unbounded. Trading an invisible risk for a visible, small, recurring one is a good trade.
72	
73	**The test.** Where did the logic I removed actually go? A move has one implementation; only a duplication risks divergence. If I wrote new behavior beside an existing upstream path rather than calling it, upstream's future improvements will never reach our users.
74	
75	**Violation.** Writing a second object-duplication routine next to OrcaSlicer's clipboard path and pointing an existing dialog at it. Reusing the existing path — extending it where it was too narrow — keeps one implementation.
76	
77	### 7. Unavoidable conflicts must be easy to resolve correctly
78	
79	**Rule.** When you must delete or relocate an upstream line, say at the site what moved, where it went, and what a future rebase must carry across.
80	
81	**Mechanism.** The real cost of a conflict is not the stop; it is the chance of resolving it wrongly. Appending near an upstream line yields a conflict whose obvious resolution — keep both — is right. Deleting an upstream line yields a conflict whose obvious resolution — take mine, the logic moved — silently discards whatever upstream did to that line in the meantime.
82	
83	**The test.** Six months from now, is the natural resolution of the conflict I am creating the correct one? If not, what does the resolver need to read to get it right, and is that text next to the conflict?
84	
85	**Violation.** Removing an upstream snapshot label that upstream later localized. Git stops for a human, but the intent-faithful resolution throws the translation away, and nothing at the site says otherwise.
86	
87	### 8. Do not diverge where you gain nothing; converge where upstream already went
88	
89	**Rule.** No gratuitous formatting, reordering, or whitespace differences. Before reverting a cosmetic difference, compare against current upstream — it may have made the same change.
90	
91	**Mechanism.** Every valueless difference is a conflict site that buys nothing. And if upstream has independently arrived at your version, "fixing" it back creates divergence rather than removing it. Adopting a change upstream has already made converges the two trees early and makes the eventual conflict resolve itself.
92	
93	**The test.** Does this difference carry meaning? Has upstream already made it?
94	
95	**Violation.** Consuming a shared blank line in a list of build subdirectories, where upstream also appends entries.
96	
97	### 9. Verify the risk claim instead of reasoning about it
98	
99	**Rule.** Before asserting that a change is or is not rebase-risky, check it. Three checks, each one command: does git actually conflict there; has upstream already converged on the same change; is the change a move or a duplication.
100	
101	**Mechanism.** A coherent story about fork risk is not a true one, and every one of these is cheaper to check than to argue about. Reasoning alone reliably produces confident, wrong claims — that a lost change is "silent" when git stops for it, that a move is a "duplication," that a cosmetic difference is gratuitous when upstream shares it.
102	
103	**The test.** Did I run the simulation, or am I describing what I expect it to say?
104	
105	**Violation.** A report that lists which files are rebase-sensitive and calls the change narrow, without having run the merge simulation that would have found two lossy resolutions waiting in it.
106	
107	### 10. Pull direction dominates every local edit
108	
109	**Rule.** Replay the fork's own commits onto upstream. Never merge upstream in, and never rebase the whole branch.
110	
111	**Mechanism.** The fork's own footprint is small; the inherited release-branch history is not. Merging upstream in makes the conflict surface the entire divergence between the release branch and upstream's development line — none of it ours. Rebasing only our commits discards that inherited history by taking upstream's version of every file we never touched.
112	
113	**The test.** Am I replaying our commits onto upstream, or bringing upstream into ours?
114	
115	**Violation.** `git merge upstream/main`, which produces a conflict list dominated by vendor profiles, translations, and CI files that JusPrin has never edited.
116	
117	## Before you finish
118	
119	A change that touches upstream-owned files is not done until this is recorded in the handback or pull request:
120	
121	1. **The rebase simulation and its result.** Run it against current upstream and name both endpoint commits — measurements are not reproducible otherwise.
122	
123	   ```bash
124	   git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=<fork base> upstream/main HEAD
125	   ```
126	
127	   For each conflicted file, state whether the natural resolution is correct or lossy. A lossy one is a defect to fix now, not a note for later.
128	
129	2. **An account of every upstream line deleted or rewritten.** Where the logic went, and why an additive form was not possible.
130	
131	3. **A statement of what the fork now owns.** Policy, a neutral seam, or upstream behavior. The third needs an explicit justification.
132	
133	An automatic merge is evidence about today's text. It is not proof that a future rebase will merge, and never proof that the merged result behaves correctly. After every upstream update, run the focused contract tests, the full native build, the real multi-plate workflow, native gizmo input, and the stock-behavior regression checks.
134	
135	## This fork's terrain
136	
137	Facts specific to OrcaSlicer, worth knowing before choosing where to put a seam. They change over time; re-measure rather than trusting these.
138
